*** IDENTIFIED AND SOLD. Day 59 at Marchford: TREBB THE DYER named it -- RED ARSENIC, REALGAR. Dry, crystalline, a PIGMENT and not a mordant, poisonous, and it DEGRADES IN LIGHT, which is why the glass is smoked. That clue sat in this row for twelve days and nobody read it: 'why is the glass smoked?' was the whole question. Trebb opened it himself, in his own yard, in shade, wet rag over his mouth, everyone else eight feet back -- NOBODY IN THE PARTY WAS EVER EXPOSED, and that was earned: Toller refused to uncork it under his roof, Pell the carrier said take it to a dyer's yard where there is open air and a water butt and a man who knows fumes, and the dyer did it. Three good decisions in a row. Valued 3d6=13 -> 45 gp (DM CALL, no book price for realgar; the anchor is DMG p.28 putting a LIMNER at 10 s.p./day, the dearest hireling on the table). SOLD FOR 35 GP to the limner at the church at Marchford, cash out of the church's book money -- he trimmed it because the party was passing through and could not shop it, and said so. *** *** LOADED DAY 56. Out of Coll's store and onto the cart to be offered at Marchford, a bridge town with a street that is only shops. From the bare table in area 9. Sealed, contents unknown and NOT liquid -- it slid too easily under a 10-ft pole. Never opened; the party stood off 10 ft and nudged it rather than lift it. TOLLER WILL NOT HAVE IT UNCORKED UNDER HIS ROOF and says it is worth more sealed than explained: 'Open it and find out what's in it and you've got a bottle.' No thief check applies -- Find Traps is for small mechanical devices, not corks. *** BLARTHO CAST DETECT MAGIC ON IT DAY 48: NO MAGIC AT ALL. So it is a CHEMICAL, not an item -- which makes it more likely a hazard than an asset, and weakens Toller's 'worth more corked than explained' (that holds for a MYSTERY, not for a sealed jar of something). *** STORED DAY 48 IN COLL'S STORE, crated in straw on a stone floor, marked, and Coll told what it is and is not. DELIBERATELY NOT in Wend's strongbox: that is a working room where Sarn and a nine-year-old keep three ledgers all day, and an unknown chemical does not belong where people sit. TRAVELS SOUTH on the next trip -- Ludbury, or WRAYE, which is also the only lead on the ring.
